title: Promotion-signal Driven Quality Prober with Contextual Sampling and Cost Caps
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Automatically run targeted quality probes whenever a model promotion signal occurs (catalog promotion OR tenant-level model promotion/lock). Deliver a policy-driven prober that composes lightweight canaries, tenant-contextual sampling, and a cost cap to ensure signal fidelity without runaway evaluation spend.

Scope:
- Trigger points: catalog promotions, customer/tenant model pin/upgrades, and config-level changes that affect serving (e.g., quantization_profile, kv_cache_policy).
- Prober composition: small suite of synthetic and sampled real-traffic probes (smoke, fidelity QA, safety checks) chosen according to promotion type and tenant profile.
- Sampling: tenant-aware sampling prioritizing high-traffic/paid tenants for more exhaustive checks and using stratified sampling across request types for catalog promotions.
- Cost controls: per-trigger token/compute budget with throttles and a global daily eval cap.
- Decisioning: scoring function that emits PASS / FLAG_FOR_REVIEW / FAIL with suggested rollback confidence and recommended fallback model variant.
- Integrations: catalog service (promotion webhook), tenant-version service (lock events), eval orchestrator, Console UI (preflight summary + one-click rollback), telemetry (observability dashboards + alerting), and webhooks to notify customer teams.

Acceptance criteria:
1) On a catalog promotion event, the prober runs a configured suite within 10 minutes and reports a PASS/FLAG/FAIL to the catalog activity log.
2) On a tenant pin/upgrade, the prober selects tenant-contextual sample (0.1% baseline, configurable per-tenant) and returns a summarized delta against the tenant's golden prompts within 30 minutes for most tenants.
3) The system enforces per-trigger cost caps; exceeding budget will pause sampling and mark the run as PARTIAL with a cost-exhausted flag.
4) Console shows preflight results with top 10 failure examples and a one-click rollback option that integrates with model-routing policies.
5) Metrics emitted: pass_rate, delta_metric (e.g., BLEU/EM/QA_accuracy depending on eval), median_latency_change, token_cost_estimate, samples_evaluated.

Design trade-offs and notes:
- Lightweight sampled evals vs full-fidelity heavy evals: default is sampled to balance speed/cost; critical tenants can opt into exhaustive checks.
- Live-traffic sampling introduces risk of customer-visible regressions during probing; we will sample on a copy stream or use replicated requests where feasible.
- Cost caps require conservative defaults and a dynamic controller to avoid starving critical probes.

Implementation outline:
1) New "promotion-prober" worker in eval-orchestrator with policy DSL for probe composition.
2) Event adapters: catalog-webhook -> prober; tenant-lock-producer -> prober.
3) Sampling library extension: tenant-priority weights + request-type stratifier.
4) Cost controller: budget ledger + throttling API.
5) Console UX: preflight modal and history card on model and tenant pages.
6) Alerts: automatic PagerDuty trigger for FAIL with high-customer-impact tenants.

Rollout plan:
- Spike (2 weeks): implement prober prototype with synthetic smoke + simple sampling; validate on internal catalog promos.
- Pilot (3 weeks): enable for 10 opt-in tenants (mix of free and paid) and run daily for catalog promos.
- Broad opt-in (4 weeks): default-on for catalog promos with opt-out for tenants; allow enterprise tenants to opt into exhaustive mode.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Promotion+Prober+Design
- Spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orchestrator/pull/3412
- Console mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ProberConsoleMockups
- Preliminary benchmark: https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/2026-02-prober-spike

Open questions:
- Do we allow promotion-prober to auto-block catalog promotion on FAIL, or only flag and require manual rollback? (proposal: flag+auto-block gated by an explicit enterprise contract).
- How to set tenant sampling defaults for small tenants to still surface regressions without excessive cost?
